verdict.summary: Issue #216 remains blocked at verified version 52f37a039ee0263c17bfb0935a85f1cd9847eba1e16a5af8b4e654419ee94662. Its owner-authored contract still lacks bounded metadata and documentation scope, verified dependency mapping, objective acceptance evidence, and explicit failure and rollout behavior. Contributor comments preserve these unresolved questions but do not authorize answers or amend the contract.

blockingFindings.title: Authoritative metadata ownership and layering are undefined
blockingFindings.details: The requirement for one authoritative root package.json and consistent package-local metadata does not identify which fields belong at the root, which may remain package-local, how conflicting values are resolved, or which packages and metadata surfaces are in scope. This prevents single-lane implementation and objective review without an owner-approved field and layering contract.

blockingFindings.title: Documentation scope and authority dispositions are unspecified
blockingFindings.details: The issue does not inventory the affected root and package documentation, state the required keep, relocate, retire, or remove disposition for each artifact, or provide the exact PRD.md and PLAN.md precedence wording. Determining which documents compete with authority is a semantic and potentially destructive owner decision.

blockingFindings.title: Dependencies and inherited scope are unverifiable
blockingFindings.details: The issue says it replaces closed issue #178 and follows #179, but it does not identify the verified #179 revision or map every inherited #178 requirement to completed evidence or remaining work. Trusted policy forbids silently treating prior work as superseded, so dependencies, residual scope, and single-lane ownership cannot be established.

blockingFindings.title: Acceptance criteria are subjective and non-testable
blockingFindings.details: Terms such as internally consistent, align, and no stale competing authority remains are not reduced to observable end-state assertions. The contract must specify the expected metadata surfaces, prohibited residue patterns, required authority references, and evidence that demonstrates each acceptance condition.

blockingFindings.title: Validation, failure handling, and rollout are missing
blockingFindings.details: The issue provides no non-executing inspection plan for metadata and documentation coverage, no fail-closed behavior for ambiguous or conflicting artifacts, and no compatibility, migration, or rollout requirements for consumers of moved or retired metadata and documentation. The independent Validate gate does not supply this missing specification coverage.

nonBlockingNotes: Owner decision required: define authoritative root versus package-local metadata fields, affected packages, and conflict precedence.
Owner decision required: inventory affected documentation, choose each artifact's disposition, and approve exact PRD.md/PLAN.md precedence wording.
Owner decision required: identify the verified #179 prerequisite revision and map all #178 requirements to completed evidence or remaining scope without declaring them superseded.
Owner decision required: approve objective end-state assertions and the evidence expected for each acceptance condition.
Owner decision required: specify ambiguity handling, compatibility or migration obligations, and rollout expectations.
